title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is the end of a computation started on the previous page (p.22 of the manuscript). The setting is Grothendieck's study of the Galois action on the Teichmüller tower in genus 0. The data are an element λ, apparently in the abelianised or scalar part (the χ / Ẑ^* component), and an element ξ' of the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. Three operators act on them: σ_∞, an involution (e.g. the symmetry swapping 0 and 1 and fixing ∞); ε_0; and ρ, the order-3 rotation of {0,1,∞}.

On the previous page Grothendieck builds β' = ξ_1 σ_∞(ξ')^{-1}. He records three equivalent expressions for it, (75) and (75'), and derives (77): σ_∞(β')^{-1} = α' σ_∞(λ), where α' = ξ' ρ(ξ')^{-1}. He then shows that the condition (72b) is equivalent to the 'two-cycle' relation (78): β' σ_∞(β') = 1. Combined with (77), this lets one simply set (79): β' = α' σ_∞(λ).

This page states the conclusion. The relation to impose on the pair (λ, ξ') can be phrased in two ways:
- the equality between β' defined by the equivalent formulas (75)/(75') and β' defined by (77); or
- equation (78), with β' defined by any one of these formulas, or by (79). Grothendieck says (79) gives 'the simplest formulation'.

In modern terms, he is reducing the constraints on a candidate element (λ, f) of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group to the two-cycle relation f·σ(f) = 1, i.e. f(x,y) f(y,x) = 1, expressed through the three-cycle quantity α' = ξ' ρ(ξ')^{-1}. This is bookkeeping toward the GT-type relations (later Drinfeld 1990, Ihara).
errors: The equation numbers on this page are written '(7б)', which look like (75)/(75') given the previous page; there is no (76) visible there. This is a numbering ambiguity, not a mathematical error.

On the previous page, 'β_1 = β'' is not deduced from (**) alone. It follows from the definition β_1 = σ_∞(β')^{-1} together with (78). This is a minor logical shortcut in the write-up, not a substantive error.

ideas.what: Reduction of the compatibility conditions on (λ, ξ') to a single two-cycle relation β' σ_∞(β') = 1, with β' expressed via the three-cycle element α' = ξ' ρ(ξ')^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Two-cycle (involution) relation f(x,y)f(y,x)=1 defining the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (in relation with the three-cycle relation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990); Ihara (1990s) for the profinite GT group
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches the genus-0 Teichmüller tower and the role of the two- and three-element relations, but contains no explicit formula of this kind

deep.surprise_reason: This is a short concluding remark selecting the simplest equivalent form of a relation computed on the preceding page. It is consistent with the known GT relations and adds no new content.
transcription_corrections: The references '(76), ou (76')' are most likely '(75), ou (75')' (the handwriting gives 7б; the previous page numbers them 75 and 75'). The same applies to '(76), ou (77)' in the fifth line, which is likely '(75), ou (77)'.
In line 1, the crossed-out phrase is 'par cette équation'; the interlinear insertion above it reads 'par les formules équivalentes'.
The crossed-out line reads approximately 'le fait que β' (ou', consistent with the transcription.
